sections.title: The High Priestly Prayer
observations: In this chapter, Jesus prays for Himself, His disciples, and all believers. This prayer is often referred to as the High Priestly Prayer, as it reflects Jesus' role as our mediator.
Jesus begins by asking the Father to glorify Him so that He may glorify the Father. This sets the tone for the prayer, emphasizing the mutual glorification between the Father and the Son.
He acknowledges the authority given to Him over all flesh, indicating His divine sovereignty and the purpose of His mission.

sections.title: Prayer for His Disciples
observations: Jesus shifts His focus to His disciples, praying for their protection and sanctification. He asks the Father to keep them in His name, highlighting the importance of unity among believers.

The request for sanctification through the truth underscores the necessity of God's Word in the life of a believer. Jesus identifies Himself as the truth, reinforcing the idea that knowing Him is essential for spiritual growth.
He acknowledges the challenges His disciples will face in the world, yet He emphasizes that they are not of the world, which calls for a distinct lifestyle.

sections.title: Prayer for All Believers
observations: In the final section, Jesus extends His prayer to all future believers, emphasizing the importance of unity among all who will come to faith through the message of the apostles.
He prays that they may be one, just as He and the Father are one. This unity is not merely organizational but is rooted in the relational nature of the Trinity.
The purpose of this unity is so that the world may believe that the Father sent the Son, highlighting the missional aspect of the church's witness.

importantVerses.commentary: Jesus prays for His glorification, which is essential for understanding His mission and the nature of His relationship with the Father.
Sanctify them in the truth; your word is truth. This verse emphasizes the role of Scripture in the believer's life.
That they may all be one, just as you, Father, are in me, and I in you. This verse highlights the importance of unity in the body of Christ.

questions: What does it mean for Jesus to be glorified, and how does that relate to His mission?
How can believers today live out the call to unity that Jesus emphasizes in His prayer?
In what ways does the truth of God's Word sanctify believers, and how can we engage with it more deeply?
